newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CEZ agrees revenue sharing deal-minister.
newsitem.headline: CEZ agrees revenue sharing deal-minister.

text.p: The main Czech electrical utility CEZ a.s. has concluded a general price and revenue sharing agreement with eight regional power distributors, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Monday.
He told a news conference the agreement sets up a long-term formula for caluculating the price CEZ charges the distributors for the power its plants produce on a yearly basis.

"We have reached an agreement on the distribution price," Dlouhy told reporters, but said the actual price CEZ would charge distributors retroactively and for the rest of 1996 would be announced "in the following days".
The long-debated issue has clouded the long-term profit outlook of CEZ, the Czech Republic's second-most highly capitalised company.
CEZ had been negotiating separate pricing deals individually with some of the distributors while awaiting a general agreement.

Dlouhy said the general agreement -- forged between a central energy board made up of representatives of CEZ, the distributors, and government officials -- would be "hard to accept for some of the distributors".
He declined to elaborate, and officials from CEZ were not immediately available for comment.
Dlouhy said he thought the "more important" aspect of the agreement was that it sets up an algorhythm for calculating the CEZ's price to the distributors.
He said in an "ideal situation", CEZ's 1997 price to the distributors would be announced "by the first of January or at the latest the first February".
